html:
Microsoft 365

The microsoft365 skill operates live Outlook mail, calendars, personal contacts, OneDrive and authorized SharePoint libraries through Microsoft Graph v1.0. Enable Microsoft 365 in the existing Capability Policy. Installing it does not change saved capability snapshots or request consent. Microsoft remains the source of truth; there is no mailbox mirror, file index, crawler or background token poll.

Register and connect

Create your own application in Microsoft Entra App registrations. Choose supported account types deliberately: a tenant UUID/domain, organizations, consumers, or common. SMTO never changes a tenant to common. The implementation supports the global Microsoft cloud, not national-cloud endpoints or app-only/client-credentials access. Work/school and personal accounts can use the supported delegated resources; SharePoint site search and multi-user free/busy require work/school accounts.

In Parameter Store, select Microsoft OAuth App. Enter the registration's client ID, tenant, and client type:

  • public: register the exact http://localhost:8400/oauth/callback URI as a mobile/ desktop redirect. The controller binds that loopback port during consent. You may configure another explicit localhost port. Use a browser on the controller machine. No client secret is needed or accepted for this type.
  • confidential: register a Web redirect such as https://your-controller/api/agent/microsoft365/oauth/callback, and save the private client secret. Local development may use an HTTP localhost/127.0.0.1 callback. The browser must reach that controller. Reverse-proxy URL reconstruction must match the registered URI exactly. SPA redirects are not supported.

Use the normal Agent or the connection tool:

{"auth_app_ref":"microsoft_app","account_key":"work_microsoft","features":["mail_read"]}

microsoft365.connect returns an expiring same-origin link. Open it and approve Microsoft's consent screen. The shared Auth browser lifecycle creates random state, PKCE S256 and OIDC nonce, consumes state once, and expires it after ten minutes. The provider verifies the signed ID token (issuer, audience, lifetime, nonce, tenant and object ID), then requires Graph /me to return that same object. Only then does Parameter Store receive the account. Microsoft app registration/tenant policy can require administrator consent even for delegated requests.

OAuth protocol and JWT verification reuse the existing Auth implementation. A separate MSAL credential cache is not installed. Browser handshakes remain private memory; Parameter Store remains the sole token authority. Public profiles and account results omit access tokens, refresh tokens and client secrets regardless of optional redaction settings. The normal explicit Parameter Store credential-editing workflow remains the operator's configuration surface.

Features and delegated scopes

Verified against Microsoft Learn on 2026-10-01. Each feature requests the following scope, in addition to identity/session scopes openid, profile, offline_access and User.Read. Mail.Read and Calendars.Read are needed for this skill's body reads; metadata-only permissions such as Mail.ReadBasic/Calendars.ReadBasic do not cover the whole respective read feature.

Feature Requested delegated Graph scope
mail_read Mail.Read
mail_write Mail.ReadWrite
mail_send Mail.Send
calendar_read Calendars.Read
calendar_write Calendars.ReadWrite
contacts_read Contacts.Read
contacts_write Contacts.ReadWrite
files_read Files.Read
files_write Files.ReadWrite
sharepoint_read Sites.Read.All
sharepoint_write Sites.ReadWrite.All

Mailbox write authority does not permit sending. OneDrive grants do not permit site discovery. Existing broader read/write grants can satisfy their corresponding read feature; new requests never silently add those broader grants. The actual token response determines stored granted_scopes and derived authorized_features.

To add access, explicitly call connect again with the same app and account_key and the additional features. Consent includes the previously granted scopes so an upgrade does not accidentally remove existing authority. A different signed-in tenant/user cannot overwrite that account. Refreshes serialize per database/account, retain an omitted refresh token, persist rotated refresh tokens, and use revision-fenced writes. Revoked refresh authorization requires reconnecting.

accounts and connection_status expose safe identity, feature and expiry metadata. They distinguish configured accounts from authorization and do not claim a network probe. Use exact account_ref when several accounts qualify. Accepted Parameter Store bindings take precedence over the unique-account convenience; an explicit account with missing permission is never substituted. Exactly one eligible account may be selected when no identity is supplied. disconnect clears local tokens and grants but does not revoke Microsoft's remote consent. Remove the profile using Parameter Store when desired.

Discovery and operations

Entry tools are accounts, connect, mail_search, calendar_events, file_search. All IDs below have the microsoft365. prefix. Discover the relevant bounded section.

Section Tool suffixes
connection accounts, connect, connection_status, disconnect
mail_read mail_folders, mail_search, mail_read_message, mail_read_conversation, mail_attachments, mail_download_attachment
mail_write mail_create_draft, mail_update_draft, mail_delete_draft, mail_send_draft, mail_send, mail_reply, mail_reply_all, mail_forward, mail_move, mail_copy, mail_mark_read, mail_flag, mail_delete
calendar_read calendars, calendar_events, calendar_read_event, calendar_availability
calendar_write calendar_create_event, calendar_update_event, calendar_delete_event, calendar_cancel_event, calendar_respond
contacts_read contact_folders, contact_search, contact_read
contacts_write contact_create, contact_update, contact_delete
files_read drives, sites_search, file_list, file_search, file_info, file_download, file_copy_status
files_write file_upload, folder_create, file_move, file_copy, file_delete

Lists return one page, default 25 and maximum 100 items, plus cursor, has_more and complete. Continue with the same account, operation, filters and limit. Opaque cursors expire after 15 minutes or service restart; Graph nextLink URLs are never model context. There is no automatic mailbox/site traversal. Individual strings and nested collections are bounded; JSON provider responses are limited to 2 MiB and mail/event bodies to 50,000 characters. Bodies are plain text, including text extracted from HTML with script/style contents removed. Search returns previews rather than all message bodies.

Mail search accepts structured sender, recipient, subject, date, read-status and attachment filters. Free query uses Graph search syntax and cannot be mixed with the structured filters; folder scope and pagination remain available. Draft creation accepts conversation-owned artifact attachments. Draft updates edit content/recipients; replace an attachment set by creating and reviewing a new draft. Send exact reviewed draft IDs. Direct send/reply/reply-all/forward require Mail.Send. Delete uses Graph's normal deletion semantics; no permanent-delete or unbounded bulk tool is exposed.

Contacts are personal Outlook contacts, including folder-scoped searches. Duplicate names remain distinct exact contact IDs. No directory-wide permission or deduplication model is used.

Calendar time and recurrence

Supply start, end, and timezone together for event time changes. List windows are bounded to 366 days. IANA timezone identifiers are supported through the controller's timezone database. The Windows aliases in calendar.WINDOWS cover UTC, major North American zones, London, Berlin, Paris, India, China, Japan, Singapore, Sydney, Auckland and Johannesburg; for other Windows names, supply the equivalent IANA identifier.

DST gaps are rejected. Repeated local times require an explicit matching UTC offset. Ordinary appointments retain the named zone; an explicitly selected repeated-time occurrence is sent in UTC to preserve the selected instant. Daily/weekly recurrence retains local wall-clock time across DST, takes an interval and exactly one of count or until, and requires weekdays for weekly patterns. Recurring boundaries at a DST fold are rejected because Graph's wall-clock recurrence cannot retain that fold choice.

For all-day events use dates, is_all_day=true, the explicit timezone and an exclusive end date. Read results retain series-master/occurrence identity; changes act only on the exact ID supplied. calendar_cancel_event invokes organizer cancellation; calendar_respond supports accept/tentative/decline. Attendees and online meeting creation are explicit inputs. Online meeting metadata uses the event API, not Teams chat/channel permissions.

calendar_availability returns structured free/busy, not scheduling advice. Graph's getSchedule supports organization accounts, at most 20 attendees and a window shorter than 62 days. Personal accounts should inspect calendar_events for their own availability.

OneDrive, SharePoint and artifacts

File operations default to the signed-in user's OneDrive. Supply exact drive_id, site_id, item_id and parent IDs for other resources. A supplied site and drive must identify the same SharePoint site. Site access is limited by both the delegated grant and the signed-in user's provider permissions; do not infer access from a site name. Moving files acts within the selected drive; copying can specify a destination drive.

Downloads stream into sensitive conversation-owned artifacts. Attachment downloads are limited to 25 MiB; cloud downloads/uploads to 250 MiB (subject also to artifact quotas). Filenames are reduced to safe leaf names with Windows reserved-name handling. No binary payload is returned inline to the Agent. Download redirects and upload session URLs stay private and receive no Graph bearer header. Transfers accept only pinned global Microsoft provider host families.

Upload sources must be artifact:// or artifact-workspace:// references in the current conversation. Register files from another Gateway through the existing artifact/Gateway handoff first. Source bytes are checked against the artifact's size and SHA-256. Up to 4 MiB uses a single content upload; larger files use a Graph upload session with 3.125 MiB chunks (multiples of 320 KiB). A lost intermediate chunk is continued only if session status proves its accepted offset. Sessions are not persisted across restarts. Mail's JSON attachments are limited to 3 MiB total.

Uploads fail on name conflicts by default. Explicit replacement requires an observed ETag and uses the existing unsafe-action authority in addition to ordinary write confirmation. File moves/updates/deletes read current ETags and use conditional requests where the provider supplies them. A stale supplied ETag fails before writing; a provider 412 is reported distinctly. This protects against intervening changes after readback, not semantic conflicts in user intent.

Copies are asynchronous: file_copy returns copy_pending and an opaque copy_handle. Poll file_copy_status; do not restart the copy. Public sharing-link creation, permission changes, SharePoint crawling, Teams messaging and bulk operations are outside this surface.

Failure and effect semantics

Tools declare external read/write effects. Connect/disconnect and all mutations require the existing native confirmation policy; the skill adds no second confirmation dialog. GETs and the read-only getSchedule POST may retry twice for transport failure, throttling or selected 5xx. Retry-After is honored; delays over 30 seconds are returned for later retry rather than shortened. A definite 401 permits one synchronized refresh. Each HTTP exchange has a 60-second hard socket deadline; a tool's transfer client has a 15-minute total ceiling and observes native cancellation.

A transport failure or 5xx after a mutation may mean the effect happened. Such writes are never generically retried. Desired-state PATCH operations can be read back to prove the supplied fields. Event creation returns its transaction ID when the result is unknown. Send acceptance is not proof of delivery, and a lost send response is never reported as successful delivery. Unknown results carry native unknown_effect receipts, so the runtime's existing replay guard blocks repeated identical calls. Inspect Sent Items, the exact resource or transaction evidence before authorizing another action.

Canonical microsoft365.* errors distinguish missing app/account, ambiguity, scope, tenant/identity mismatch, invalid consent state, revoked authorization, forbidden sites, 404, conflict, precondition failure, throttling, invalid timezones, transfer bounds and unknown effects. Consult the generated error manual or the returned remediation. Provider messages, tokens, authorization headers, raw codes/verifiers and full response bodies are excluded from diagnostics. Microsoft tool content participates in the shared structural content-omission policy; credential reflection is redacted unconditionally. Mail, calendar text, contacts and file metadata remain untrusted external data. Only the normal Agent interprets it. Provider authentication, shaping, retries and reconciliation make zero helper-model calls.

References and verification

Microsoft references checked on 2026-10-01:

  • Authorization code and PKCE, MSAL Python token acquisition.
  • Delegated permissions, mail lists, draft send.
  • Calendar view, getSchedule, timezones.
  • Contacts, file search, site search.
  • Downloads, upload sessions, asynchronous copy.
  • Throttling, error responses.

Mandatory tests use signed fake OAuth, deterministic Graph fixtures, a local HTTP server and real desktop/mobile UI surfaces. No live tenant is required. Optional live testing must use a dedicated test account/tenant and disposable resources; never run destructive checks on a developer's personal mailbox, calendar or OneDrive.
